subject: Energy
title: Nuclear Power for Mars
description: One-minute skill: Nuclear Power for Mars.

hook.text: Solar power on Mars is only 40% as strong as on Earth—dust storms can block sunlight for months.

buildup.text: NASA's Curiosity rover uses a plutonium RTG (radioisotope generator)—providing steady power for over a decade.

discovery.text: A Mars base would need megawatts—far beyond RTGs, requiring small fission reactors like NASA's Kilopower concept.

twist.text: Kilopower uses a uranium core the size of a paper towel roll—generating 10 kW, enough for a small habitat.

climax.text: SpaceX envisions cities on Mars powered by solar plus nuclear—energy infrastructure is essential for any Mars colony.

punchline.text: No grid on Mars—nuclear reactors will power the first colonies.

quiz.question: Why is solar power less effective on Mars?
options: Sunlight is weaker and dust storms block it
Mars is too cold for panels
